recipes.name: Taco Soup IV
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: In a medium stock pot brown beef and onion, about 10 minutes; drain grease if needed.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce, water, beans, corn and taco seasoning. Bring to boil, reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Top with cheese, corn chips, sour cream and olives.

raw_recipe.headline: Taco Soup IV
raw_recipe.description: Ground beef, onion, pinto beans and corn are combined with a packet of taco seasoning mix in this soup served with sour cream, grated cheese, sliced black olives and corn chips.

review.reviewBody: This is a great basic taco soup recipe! To lengthen how far this goes add an extra can of tomatoe sauce, another cup of water, omit 1 pound of ground beef, add 1-2 more cans of rinsed, drained beans and more taco seasoning to taste.I also never use corn and sub in-you guessed it-more beans! I typically use these 3 beans in one batch- red kidney beans, garbanzo beans and black beans. But ANY bean will work here! Kick the flavor up by adding a small well drained can of diced green chilis and chopped olives. Put a dollop of sour cream and small handful shredded chedder in each bowl just before serving. Don't forget the hot sauce on the side for heat lovers! Thanks Patricia for such a fun, versatile recipe!

This is now my favorite soup! I was looking for a recipe to use tomato puree I had drained off a big can of tomatoes I was drying to make raw ketchup (which didn't turn out). I omitted the tomato sauce so I could use more puree. So I had to add extra spices. I just kept tasting and adding until it was right! My family doesn't care for onions, but I do use onion powder and I did put in a couple dashes of garlic. I also added more beans and some leftover rice. All that to say this is a great basic recipe that can be tweaked to your taste!

After reading other reviews, I subbed 1 qt homemade tomato puree + 1 cup of water for the puree and sauce called for, along with 1 put of homemade chicken bone broth. I used 4 Tbsp of homemade taco seasoning (another allrecipes recipe - 2 tbsp per pound of beef) and I used 1 drained can of organic black beans and one of organic kidney beans (I'm not a fan of pintos). I also used a couple of handfuls of frozen corn instead of the canned corn. I mixed guacamole into the bowls of soup and it was SO good. My husband said this is his new favorite soup recipe. Thanks so much, I'm sure this is going to be a new frequent favorite in our home.
Used beef broth instead of water, black beans instead of pinto and added a dash of chili powder. Hearty and delicious! My sons ate it with Fritos Scoops. Moving this to our Favorites!!!!

This more like a thick Chili rather than a soup. Very easy to put together and can easily be adapted to what you have on hand. I agree with another reviewer. Cooked the meat (drain the grease if there is any) and added the taco seasoning to the meat and onions - stir and cook that for a bit before adding the other ingredients. You could add broth, diced green chilies, carrots, zucchini, cabbage - but that would be a different recipe, wouldn't it?

Great recipe, used Ranch style beans instead of plain pinto beans. Added more tomatoes. Simmered a bit longer and added 8 cups of water to make it more soup like. Served with sour cream and fritos. Awesome leftovers.

I used this recipe to use up some vegetables in my fridge. So, I added celery, carrots, green pepper & cabbage. I didn't have beef so I just used some stewing beef. The whole thing was put in the crock pot. It was delicious.

I always add the taco seasoning to the ground round just after it has browned.. makes a diff. somehow. Also add a chopped green or yellow bell pepper. Carrots would be good too, as a poster mentioned below.

This was a good and easy soup that uses ground beef, but I substituted Johnsonville mild Italian sausage for the beef. I removed the casings and broke it up with a wooden spoon while cooking. It was really good!
very basic recipe, i added green chiles,fresh jalapenos,garlic, rotel, red pepper,cumin and finelly hominy, it sounded good in there....

This is a good recipe when you are tired of the regular tacos. It's also a good busy weeknight meal when you don't have a lot of time to spend on dinner. I found that this is more like a chili than a soup, and I added about 1.5 cups of chicken broth I had to use up and a can of water to thin it out some more. Even with all that extra liquid, it was still pretty thick. I also added about 2 cloves of chopped garlic, and extra chili powder and cumin, since one taco packet will flavor only 1 lb. of ground beef. I served this by breaking some tortilla chips in the bottom of the bowls, adding the soup and topping with shredded cheese and sour cream. Everyone enjoyed this, and I will make it again! Thanks!
Very good, doubled everything except the beef and added beef boullion until desired consistency. Really great flavor!
Everyone enjoyed it and went for seconds. That's a pretty good indication.
This was the best soup I have ever made yummy
My family loves this recipe. Everyone just grabs a BIG bowl and their favorite chips and are in heaven.
one of my favourite soups i added kidney beans and ranch dressing mix

this recipe is so good. I used to use this site a lot before pinterest and just had a taste for this taco soup. i pulled up this site and bam, there it was! i did add another cup of water and only did half the onion. my coworkers loved it too. i will for sure make this for a party
This was good, but not great. Perfect recipe for quick, throw-together meal. It was hearty and comforting. However, I highly doubt I will look this recipe up again.
Just made this! It's really good. I put sour cream, mexican blend cheese, hot sauce and corn chips around the bowl. Yum!
A huge hit with the family. Added extra taco seasoning, beans and also added diced tomato's. Will be making this more this winter.
